But the reason it's breaking all sorts of box office records is simple: it makes us laugh and tremble at a truth that our time considers distinctly taboo.

It also perfectly eschews wokeness and DEI: the friend group isn't a microcosm of the U.N. general assembly, no gay stuff, etc. And the film is technically excellent: the script is tight, shots look good, solid acting.

It does lots of other issues too: the difference between love and infatuation, the misery that comes from appropriating to ourselves what properly belongs to God, imperfect contrition, the implications of marriage, etc.

"Obsession" realistically depicts the dynamic between men and women in an entertaining way during an era defined by the denial of sexual complementarity. That's the secret to its success.
